While public records show fluctuating ownership ties to Megaspeed and past senior roles at Chinese investment firms, Beijing's Foreign Ministry rejected the allegations this week as unsubstantiated smears.
articles.description: An affair between Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who reportedly was suspected of working as a spy for Beijing, has rocked the tech and political worlds

articles.headline: United States publishes report detailing management of Venezuelan oil revenues
articles.title: US releases report on $12bn from Venezuelan oil, mineral resources
articles.summary: The United States Department of State released a report on Thursday detailing the distribution of more than twelve billion dollars generated from Venezuelan oil and mineral resources following the removal of former leader Nicolas Maduro. The funds, handled through Treasury-controlled accounts and audited by KPMG, were primarily disbursed to Venezuelan banks to support foreign exchange interventions.
articles.description: The report seeks to address concerns about the Trump administration's handling of revenue held in trust for Venezuela.

articles.headline: Indian boxers L. Ambekar Meetei and Gunjan win historic gold medals
articles.title: Ambekar, Gunjan script history with boxing gold medals at Youth Olympics
articles.summary: L. Ambekar Meetei and Gunjan secured India's first-ever boxing gold medals at the Youth Olympic Games on Thursday. Ambekar defeated Kristian Jubani in the men's fifty-kilogram final, while Gunjan defeated Bouthaina Bensalah in the women's forty-eight-kilogram division. These victories mark the nation's most successful boxing performance in the history of the international multi-sport youth competition.
articles.description: Ambekar beat Ireland’s Kristen Jubani 3-2; Gunjan won 5-0 over Algeria’s Bouthaina Bensalah, becoming India’s first-ever woman to claim a boxing gold at the Youth Olympic Games

articles.headline: Vivaan Kapoor wins silver and secures Olympic quota in trap shooting
articles.title: Vivaan Kapoor wins trap silver, secures India’s LA 2028 Olympic quota
articles.summary: Indian marksman Vivaan Kapoor secured a silver medal in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships on Thursday after a close shoot-off against Kuwait's Abdulrahman Alfaihan. The twenty-four-year-old athlete from Jaipur also earned India a quota place for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games, becoming the third Indian shooter to achieve this qualification milestone.
articles.description: Vivaan became only the fourth Indian men’s trap shooter after the legendary Karni Singh (silver), Manavjit Singh Sandhu (gold) and Zorawar Singh Sandhu (bronze in 2025) to win a medal at the World Championships in the highly competitive discipline

articles.headline: China faces economic challenges despite reaching a record one trillion dollar trade surplus
articles.title: Why China’s $1 trillion trade surplus isn’t all good news for its economy
articles.summary: China achieved a record trade surplus of one point zero four trillion dollars in the first ten months of the year, driven by strong semiconductor and tech exports. However, economists warn that chronically weak domestic demand, low household consumption, and inadequate social safety nets leave the country's export-dependent economic model vulnerable to international trade curbs and tariffs.
articles.description: Booming exports mask a thriftiness among the Chinese that could undermine long-term growth.

articles.headline: Argentina and United Kingdom clash over Falkland Islands oil drilling project
articles.title: What’s at stake in the renewed tensions over the Falkland Islands?
articles.summary: A legal dispute has emerged between Argentina and the United Kingdom concerning an oil drilling project off the coast of the Falkland Islands. The Argentinian government wants to halt operations by a joint British-Israeli venture until sovereignty is resolved, while the British government rejects these claims and maintains full sovereignty over the region. The confrontation marks the latest development in the long-running territorial dispute.
articles.description: Argentina and the UK are in a legal battle over an offshore oil-drilling project.

articles.headline: Oil tanker catches fire after striking naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: Iran says tanker struck mine, caught fire in Hormuz
articles.summary: An oil tanker caught fire on November 11, 2026, after striking a naval mine in an unauthorised area of the eastern Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's army. The incident follows severe restrictions on the strategic waterway by Tehran since the West Asia war began in February, alongside ongoing US naval blockades and escorts to protect regional oil exports.
articles.description: The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait

articles.headline: Iran security chief says Tehran is waiting for Washington to respond to peace terms
articles.title: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met
articles.summary: Iran security chief Mohsen Rezaei stated that Tehran is awaiting a response from the United States regarding seven conditions for peace talks, while dismissing reports of ongoing negotiations in Qatar. Rezaei insisted the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until demands including lifted sanctions and ending regional fighting are met, despite US President Donald Trump noting positive diplomatic momentum.
articles.description: Mohsen Rezaei's comments come as the IRGC said at least three ships had hit mines and caught fire in the Hormuz strait.

articles.headline: Nvidia confirms technical ability to track chips to fight smuggling
articles.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility
articles.summary: Representatives from Nvidia told United States Representative Bill Foster that the company could implement anti-smuggling geotracking measures for artificial intelligence chips. The disclosure follows legislative efforts in the Senate to curb illicit shipments to China. While industry groups previously claimed such tracking was infeasible, internal tools like Fleet Intelligence demonstrate location monitoring capabilities.
articles.description: Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on…

articles.headline: European leaders gather in Dublin for summit amid hybrid security threats
articles.title: Regional security dominates European talks in Dublin amid hybrid attacks
articles.summary: Leaders from more than forty European countries met in Dublin for a summit focused on regional security following a wave of hybrid attacks, cyberattacks, and hoax bomb warnings across the continent. Republic of Ireland Prime Minister Micheal Martin condemned the disruptions during the European Political Community gathering. Meanwhile, discussions also addressed potential European representation in upcoming peace talks regarding the war in Ukraine.
articles.description: European nations discuss security collaboration and an envoy for Ukraine peace talks during the summit in Ireland.

articles.headline: U.S. immigration arrests continue nationwide despite President Trump expressing midterm election misgivings
articles.title: Immigration arrests go on unabated despite Trump's misgivings after GOP's midterm wipeout
articles.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations continued nationwide following the midterm elections, with arrests reported in states including California, Florida, and Alabama. While President Donald Trump suggested his crackdown may have been too tough, Department of Homeland Security officials confirmed that deportations will proceed without interruption despite pending asylum applications and valid work permits held by some detainees.
articles.description: After Democrats trounced GOP and won control of the next Congress, Donald Trump said his immigration crackdown may have been “too tough” and suggested it was time to sit down with the rival party

articles.headline: Democrats convene in Denver for conference following midterm congressional victories
articles.title: Democrats gather in Denver to debate party’s future after US midterm wins
articles.summary: Following victories in the midterm elections, Democratic lawmakers, strategists, and potential presidential candidates gathered in Denver for a two-day conference called What’s Next. Organized by the moderate group Majority Democrats, the event aims to debate the future direction of the party as members prepare to take control of Congress in January. Attendees include prominent leaders and newly elected lawmakers discussing upcoming legislative strategies.
articles.description: Majority Democrats’ What’s Next conference brings lawmakers and potential 2028 contenders to Denver.

articles.headline: Moody's raises India's fiscal year 2027 growth forecast to 7 percent
articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.summary: Moody's Ratings on November 11, 2026, upgraded India's current fiscal year growth projection to 7 percent from 6.5 percent, citing broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience. According to the U.S.-based agency, robust consumption and strong fundamentals support the outlook, though inflation risks and monetary tightening by the Reserve Bank of India remain concerns.
articles.description: Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said

articles.headline: Court sentences relative to thirty years imprisonment for raping minor
articles.title: Kin convicted for raping minor
articles.summary: A special court in Thodupuzha trying offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act sentenced a thirty-seven-year-old man to thirty years of imprisonment for raping a minor relative. Sessions Judge Ash K. Bal delivered the verdict for the crime committed in October 2021, which included house trespass. The court additionally ordered five lakh rupees in compensation for the survivor from the victim compensation fund.

articles.headline: New Zealand defeats India five nil in international football friendly
articles.title: FIFA friendly: New Zealand hammer India 5-0 in Auckland
articles.summary: The Indian men's national football team suffered a five-nil defeat against New Zealand in an international friendly match in Auckland. Jesse Randall scored two goals, while Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss added to an early own goal by Bijoy Varghese. Despite multiple saves from Indian goalkeeper Vishal Kaith, including a second-half penalty stop, the hosts dominated the fixture ahead of their next meeting in Christchurch.
articles.description: In what was the Blue Tigers’ first-ever match in New Zealand, Jesse Randall struck a brace, while Chris Wood and Lachlan Bayliss found the net after a Bijoy Varghese own goal opened the scoring

articles.headline: US nonprofits sue major tech companies to halt artificial intelligence development
articles.title: US nonprofits sue tech giants to halt AI development
articles.summary: Four advocacy groups filed a civil lawsuit Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court demanding an emergency freeze on artificial intelligence model training and deployments by Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and SpaceX. The plaintiffs allege these tech giants violate California unfair competition law by endangering public safety. They argue federal regulation is urgently needed to prevent catastrophic harm to critical infrastructure and humanity.
articles.description: California lawsuit demands freeze training on 'catastrophic' artificial intelligence models.

articles.headline: Palaniswami dismisses speculation about readmitting Dhinakaran and Sasikala into AIADMK
articles.title: Palaniswami rejects speculation of Dhinakaran, Sasikala being readmitted into AIADMK
articles.summary: AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami dismissed questions regarding the potential readmission of AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran and former interim general secretary V.K. Sasikala. Speaking at the Chennai airport on Thursday, Palaniswami noted that both individuals have established their own separate political parties. Additionally, he asserted that his party is fully prepared for upcoming bypolls and criticized the current government's governance.

articles.headline: Minister Rajmohan states no government schools will close due to low enrollment
articles.title: No government school will be closed due to low enrolment: Minister Rajmohan
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu Minister for School Education Rajmohan announced Thursday that no state government schools will close despite low student enrollment figures. Speaking in Vellore, he highlighted new curriculum updates and storytelling math teaching methods designed to boost attendance. Meanwhile, VIT founder G. Viswanathan noted broader educational challenges, including closed schools and zero-enrollment campuses across the region over the past decade.

articles.headline: Google researcher falsely claims artificial intelligence discovery of Maya site
articles.title: No, AI agents did not discover a previously unknown Maya site
articles.summary: Google researcher Pietro Miotti utilized artificial intelligence agents to analyze NASA lidar data, claiming the discovery of an unmapped Maya site in Mexico. Archaeologists quickly disproved the claim, revealing the location was published in an academic journal last year. The incident highlights growing friction as amateurs apply advanced artificial intelligence tools to specialist fields without sufficient domain expertise or verification against existing literature.
articles.description: Armed with a team of AI agents, Google researcher Pietro Miotti claimed earlier this week to have discovered a potentially unmapped Maya site in Mexico. There was just one problem: The site had already been discovered and was published in an academic journal last year. The incident, which sparked criticism among archeologists online, underscores a […]

articles.headline: Carlos Alcaraz enters ATP finals as player to beat in Turin
articles.title: ATP finals 2026: Alcaraz has the momentum while Zverev motivated to silence critics
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz enters the season-ending tournament in Turin on a 10-match winning run following titles in Vienna and Paris, according to reports. The event starts on Sunday in Italy, featuring the top eight men's players, though two-time defending champion Jannik Sinner is sitting out due to a right knee injury. Meanwhile, top-ranked Alexander Zverev faces criticism over his ranking following injuries to competitors.
articles.description: While Zverev arrives on a two-match losing streak, Alcaraz comes to Turin on a 10-match winning run after titles in Vienna and Paris and is hungry to raise the trophy at the Finals for the first time after losing to Jannik Sinner in last year’s final

articles.headline: Iranian men guilty of spying on British journalists
articles.title: Iranian men guilty of spying on British journalists
articles.description: Two Iranian men were convicted under Britain's National Security Act for spying on dissident journalists.

articles.headline: Congo surpasses 11,000 Ebola cases in deadliest outbreak
articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
articles.summary: Congo's Health Ministry reported on November 11, 2026, that infections in the country's severe Ebola outbreak have reached 11,042, with 5,387 deaths recorded. The epidemic, declared in mid-May and driven by the Bundibugyo virus, has spread to eight provinces, presenting significant containment challenges due to ongoing regional conflicts and strained health systems.
articles.description: Since the outbreak was declared mid-May, Congolese authorities have struggled to contain it due to a series of factors including conflicts and a health system crisis

articles.headline: Chinese university procures Nvidia artificial intelligence chips despite United States ban
articles.title: Chinese university buys Nvidia AI H200 chips despite US ban, records show
articles.summary: Northwestern Polytechnical University in China purchased two restricted Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips last month for 874,700 yuan through a local supplier, according to procurement records. The military-linked institution is subject to United States export blacklist restrictions, highlighting ongoing challenges in enforcing technological controls amid broader scrutiny facing Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang.
articles.description: Investigation reveals Chinese entities accessing US-restricted AI tech despite stringent export control measures.

articles.headline: Bomb threats force fresh evacuations across Italian schools for second day
articles.title: Suspected bomb hoax threats force fresh evacuations of Italian schools
articles.summary: Educational institutions throughout Italy experienced widespread disruptions and evacuations following a second consecutive wave of threatening messages. Approximately 1,800 facilities received electronic warnings, mirroring a previous incident affecting thousands of locations. Despite the government advising against evacuations without concrete evidence, parents expressed concern and demanded clearer national guidelines while authorities investigated the origin of the coordinated false alerts.
articles.description: Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations.

articles.headline: Iran security official denies ongoing negotiations with Washington
articles.title: No talks underway with U.S., says Iran top security official
articles.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, a senior Iranian security official, stated that no direct talks are occurring between Tehran and Washington. Speaking with the broadcaster Al-Mayadeen, Rezaei noted that Iran is awaiting an explicit response from the United States regarding seven specific conditions set out in a June interim agreement before normal diplomatic channels can resume.
articles.description: Iran ‌has insisted ‌the ⁠U.S. must meet ⁠seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement ​before the ‌Strait of Hormuz can reopen and negotiations resume

articles.headline: US treasury secretary urges caution on artificial intelligence competition
articles.title: U.S. and China should stay clear-eyed on AI cooperation and competition, says Scott Bessent
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized that Washington and Beijing must remain clear-eyed regarding artificial intelligence differences while pursuing cooperation on risk mitigation. Speaking in New York ahead of an upcoming leaders summit in Shenzhen, Bessent outlined plans for a bilateral dialogue on superintelligence and new mutual evaluation practices.
articles.description: Bessent, who will travel to China next week for U.S. President Donald Trump’s third meeting this year with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said that he wanted to “build a constructive relationship on the basis of balance and reciprocity”

articles.headline: US secretary of state sees no immediate need for attacks on Iran
articles.title: Rubio says 'no need' to attack Iran as diplomacy gathers pace
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that devastating economic pressure on Iran makes major combat operations unnecessary at this stage. Following a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio emphasized that diplomacy is gaining momentum as Tehran continues urging Washington to accept its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: Tehran said its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days — if Washington agreed to a raft of conditions — remained on the table

articles.headline: Police file chargesheet against Veeramani based on minor complaint
articles.title: Veeramani chargesheet was based on plaint lodged by minor girl
articles.summary: A chargesheet submitted in a designated court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act cases targets Veeramani and two drivers following a complaint by a minor girl. Police sources stated the survivor alleged sexual exploitation and identified the businessman during a special investigation team identification process. Veeramani faces multiple cases involving more than 10 survivors, while co-accused Prakash Kanniah is believed to be in the United Kingdom.
articles.description: The survivor alleged in her complaint that she was sexually exploited by Veeramani

articles.headline: Shreyas Iyer emerges as a central figure in cricket
articles.title: Shreyas Iyer — from losing a central contract to becoming the central figure
articles.summary: Cricketers often aspire to national captaincy while facing varied career trajectories influenced by peers and timing, according to a report published on November 13, 2026. While notable tacticians like M.L. Jaisimha and V.V.S. Laxman never led India, player Shreyas Iyer has unexpectedly stepped into a major leadership role as if destined for the position.
articles.description: The 31-year-old, who has enjoyed a remarkable turnaround in the last two years, will scale another high when he leads India in the fourth one-dayer against New Zealand at Mount Maunganui; he has been an asset to the National team’s 50-over set-up for a while now

articles.headline: CPI(M) leader criticizes police action against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram
articles.title: CPI(M) leader P. Rajeeve flays police action against protesters in Keralam’s Thiruvananthapuram
articles.summary: Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader P. Rajeeve condemned Wednesday night police actions against protesters in Thiruvananthapuram and the hospitalisation of Valarmathi S., a hunger-striking action council secretary. He urged the government to specify which court order justified the crackdown and explain why it reversed assurances regarding Public Service Commission rank lists, speaking to the media on Thursday in the state.

articles.headline: Agentic artificial intelligence systems now execute independent physical tasks in biological laboratories
articles.title: Now agentic AI can perform complex lab research, and maybe cheaper too
articles.summary: Published on November 13, 2026, new artificial intelligence technology has evolved beyond digital chat interfaces to perform autonomous physical experiments. These autonomous systems can operate laboratory equipment such as pipettes and thermal cyclers to conduct, observe, document, and interpret biological research without direct human physical intervention, marking a significant shift in scientific capabilities.
articles.description: On November 4, 2026, in the journal Nature, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University presented their findings on an Agentic laboratory platform, “AutoDNA”. It is an artificial intelligence system with agents performing the function of humans who usually perform complex experiments

articles.headline: Adyar Ananda Bhavan sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree Systems
articles.title: A2B sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree in $180-million deal
articles.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan secured one hundred eighty million dollars in investments from Bodhi Tree Systems, yielding a majority stake in a deal valuing the brand at approximately three hundred fifty million dollars. Vishnu Shankar confirmed funds will modernize factories in Chennai and Bengaluru, expanding the business into western India and Europe, building on a network of roughly 160 restaurants.
articles.description: The deal values A2B at $350 million, says a source

articles.headline: Spain court to hear US extradition request for James Chambers
articles.title: Pro-Palestine philanthropist faces US extradition hearing in Spain
articles.summary: Spain's National Court will hear evidence from United States authorities on Friday regarding the extradition of James Chambers, an American philanthropist charged with money laundering and riot offenses. His wife, Stella Schnabel, urged Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to expedite an asylum claim to prevent political persecution. Defense lawyers allege mistranslations in documents submitted to Spanish authorities by the Department of Justice.
articles.description: James 'Fergie' Chambers denies wrongdoing, while his wife urges PM Sanchez to grant him political asylum.

articles.headline: Gold heist reported at Tanishq showroom in Madurai
articles.title: Major gold heist at Tanishq jewellery showroom in Madurai
articles.summary: A gold heist occurred at the TATA Tanishq showroom in Madurai on November 11, 2026. Discovered by employees on November 12, Commissioner of Police S. Rajendiran stated that a lone masked man entered through a terrace lift vent and stole display items. Security personnel were deployed outside as forensic teams and police investigated the ongoing theft assessment.
articles.description: The heist occurred on Wednesday night at the recently opened TATA Tanishq showroom on Bypass Road

articles.headline: India faces New Zealand in fourth one-day international under new captains
articles.title: Shreyas in focus on ODI captaincy debut as modified India look to seal series
articles.summary: India aims to secure the series against New Zealand in the fourth fixture on November 13, 2026, with Shreyas Iyer taking over the one-day international captaincy. Both squads face major player absences as team members transition to red-ball preparations. New Zealand trails 2-0 after the third match was abandoned, placing pressure on the touring side to avoid a series defeat.
articles.description: Leading 2-0 in the five-match series, India would back themselves to seal the series while New Zealand can only save the rubber by winning the remaining fixtures here, following the abandonment of the third ODI

articles.headline: Delhi air quality reaches very poor levels following Deepavali
articles.title: Delhi air quality deteriorates, AQI settles at 303
articles.summary: Delhi recorded a very poor air quality index of 303, according to Central Pollution Control Board data released on Wednesday. The deterioration follows post-Deepavali pollution and agricultural stubble burning in neighbouring States. Meanwhile, the Safdarjung weather station recorded a minimum temperature of 14.8 degrees Celsius, and the India Meteorological Department forecast morning fog or mist with a maximum temperature reaching 28 degrees Celsius.
articles.description: The national capital is battling rising pollution levels after Deepavali, with stubble burning in neighbouring States contributing to the deterioration

articles.headline: United States previously owned home sales drop to lowest level since 2010
articles.title: Home sales in the US are at their lowest level since 2016
articles.summary: Sales of previously owned homes in the United States decreased by 5.5 percent in October to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million units, according to the National Association of Realtors. Lawrence Yun, the organization's chief economist, attributed the decline to mortgage rates remaining above 7 percent. First-time buyers accounted for 29 percent of purchases during the month.
articles.description: The sale of previously owned homes dropped 5.5 percent in October, the lowest level since August 2010.

articles.headline: India defeats Afghanistan to reach Under-19 Asia Cup final
articles.title: U19 Asia Cup: Raichandani’s 93 sees India to final, to face Pakistan in title clash
articles.summary: Skipper Lakshya Raichandani scored 93 runs to lead India to an eight-wicket victory over Afghanistan in the Under-19 Asia Cup semifinal on November 12, 2026, in Al Amerat, Oman. The bowling attack restricted Afghanistan to 227 for eight. India advanced to face Pakistan in the title clash scheduled for November 14, 2026, after Pakistan defeated Bangladesh.

articles.headline: Gunman kills one and wounds others in Washington gym shooting
articles.title: What to know about the Logan Circle shooting in Washington, DC
articles.summary: A gunman identified as physician Matt Lambert opened fire inside a gym in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, DC, on November 12, 2026, killing one person and injuring others. Interim Police Chief Jeffery Carroll stated the attack stemmed from a housing dispute. The suspect later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound following a police standoff.
articles.description: Trump has showcased the capital city as an example of his tough-on-crime approach.

articles.headline: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu navigates political challenges as opposition builds majority
articles.title: Netanyahu fights to stay relevant as Israel’s opposition closes in
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called for a unified government amid ongoing coalition negotiations following October elections. While former Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot works to form a government holding 67 Knesset seats with parties such as United Torah Judaism, Netanyahu faces multiple corruption trials and intense political pressure regarding security failures connected to the October 7 Hamas attack. The newly sworn-in Knesset includes many members directly affected by the conflict.
articles.description: A new Knesset shaped by October 7 prepares to convene as Netanyahu fights to prevent an opposition-led government

articles.headline: Turkish military helicopter crash leaves four personnel dead in Malatya
articles.title: Military helicopter crashes in southern Turkey, killing 4
articles.summary: A military helicopter crashed in Samankoy on the southern outskirts of Malatya, Turkey, on November 12, 2026, resulting in the deaths of four personnel. The Turkish Defence Ministry announced the incident involving the S-70 aircraft, while emergency responders rushed to the scene. Television footage displayed burning wreckage near buildings, though no ground casualties were reported.
articles.description: The aircraft crashed for unknown reasons in Samankoy, a neighbourhood on the southern outskirts of the provincial capital Malatya in the evening

articles.headline: CPI demands investigation into alleged Lok Sabha election vote discrepancies
articles.title: CPI seeks probe into ‘poll discrepancies’
articles.summary: The Communist Party of India has called for a federal probe into reported discrepancies between votes polled and counted during the Lok Sabha elections. Party leaders cited findings from The Reporters' Collective regarding data in three states. The CPI plans to coordinate a nationwide movement with INDIA bloc partners to address these concerns and electoral integrity.
articles.description: Ramakrishna demands resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of favouring BJP and RSS

articles.headline: Medical exams confirm injuries to recaptured Theni jail prisoners
articles.title: Medical examination of recaptured prisoners, allegedly thrashed by Theni jail warders, confirms injuries
articles.summary: A medical examination ordered by the Madras High Court has confirmed multiple injuries on four prisoners recaptured after escaping from Theni district jail on October 26, 2026. The court is awaiting a report from the Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority regarding allegations of custodial torture. Further hearings are scheduled for November 17, 2026, in the case.
articles.description: Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan of the Madras High Court direct government doctors to provide medical treatment to the injured prisoners

articles.headline: Karnataka plans 24 GW power capacity expansion with massive investment
articles.title: Karnataka targets 24 GW power capacity in five years; plans over ₹3 lakh crore investment
articles.summary: Karnataka aims to add 24 GW of power capacity over the next five years, requiring investments exceeding ₹3 lakh crore. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced the plan ahead of the 2027 Global Investors Meet. The state is focusing on renewable energy and industrial infrastructure development in cities outside Bengaluru to address regional imbalances and promote sustainable growth.
articles.description: Global Investors Meet is scheduled to be held in Bengaluru between April 20 and 22, 2027

articles.headline: Suspect turns gun on himself after deadly shooting in Washington DC
articles.title: Suspect turns gun on himself after deadly shooting in Washington DC
articles.description: Police say the man suspected to have killed one person in a shooting in Washington DC appears to have shot himself.

articles.headline: ReNew announces ₹80,000 crore investment in Andhra Pradesh projects
articles.title: Vizag CII Summit: ReNew to invest ₹80,000 crore in green data centre, solar manufacturing in Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: ReNew Energy Global Plc will invest approximately ₹80,000 crore in Andhra Pradesh to develop a green data centre, silicon manufacturing facilities, and a magnet plant. Announced at the CII Partnership Summit 2026, the projects aim to support the state's renewable energy targets. The company will also establish a technical excellence centre in Visakhapatnam to boost local skills.
articles.description: Investments include a ₹67,000-crore Green Hyperscale Data Centre in Anakapalli, ₹11,000-crore polysilicon and metallurgical silicon manufacturing facilities in Anakapalli and Nellore; and ₹1,500-crore permanent magnet manufacturing facility in Rambilli

articles.headline: Union minister Piyush Goyal assures global investors of India's reliability
articles.title: India will remain a trusted partner for global investors, assures Union Minister Piyush Goyal
articles.summary: Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal stated that India will remain a reliable destination for foreign direct investments during the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit in Visakhapatnam. Speaking on November 12, 2026, he emphasized the country's stable policies, protection of intellectual property rights, and growing manufacturing opportunities, while praising Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu for advancing the speed of doing business.
articles.description: Amid the global uncertainties, India is doing all it can to ensure safety of the investors’ money, says the Union Minister for Commerce & Industry

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces and Houthi rebels report heavy casualties in escalating clashes
articles.title: Yemeni forces, Houthis exchange attacks, claim to inflict heavy losses
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces reported killing or injuring approximately 190 Houthi fighters during hundreds of recent air and artillery attacks across multiple governorates. Meanwhile, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed that Saudi-backed strikes on Sanaa and other areas caused numerous casualties, while reporting retaliatory Houthi missile attacks targeting Riyadh and an oil facility in Abqaiq. The World Health Organization reports thousands of casualties and widespread displacement since August amidst broader regional hostilities.
articles.description: Yemen's government says 190 rebel fighters killed and wounded, as Houthis also claim dealing heavy blows.

articles.headline: Leh Apex Body begins indefinite protest over MHA talks failure
articles.title: Ladakh civil society group begins protest over Home Ministry failure to hold talks
articles.summary: Ladakh civil society group Leh Apex Body organized an indefinite sit-in at Nawang Dorjay Stobdan Memorial Park in Leh on November 12, 2026, protesting the Ministry of Home Affairs' failure to resume talks and the scheduling of hill council elections during winter. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was placed under house arrest by the district administration under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita to prevent unauthorized gatherings.
articles.description: It opposes holding of hill council elections at the peak of winter; climate activist Sonam Wangchuk put under house arrest and disallowed to join the protest

articles.headline: Ola Electric narrows quarterly loss through restructuring and cost controls
articles.title: India's Ola Electric quarterly loss narrows on cost cuts
articles.summary: The electric vehicle manufacturer reported a consolidated loss of 3.62 billion rupees for the three months ending September 30, improving from a loss of 4.18 billion rupees previously. According to the Bhavish Aggarwal-led firm, expenses fell by 28.4% due to workforce restructuring and warranty reductions, though unit sales declined amid intense competition from rivals such as Ather Energy.
articles.description: The electric-vehicle maker reported a consolidated ‌loss of 3.62 billion rupees ($38.66 million) ​for the three months ended September ⁠30, compared with a loss of 4.18 billion rupees a year ago

articles.headline: Washington DC shooting leaves one dead and four injured
articles.title: Washington DC shooting: One dead, four people injured
articles.summary: Five individuals were shot on November 12, 2026, in the Logan Circle neighbourhood of Washington, D.C., resulting in one fatality, according to Metropolitan Police Department interim chief Jeffrey Carroll. The suspected gunman died by suicide following a standoff inside an apartment building after allegedly opening fire near a local fitness centre and parking garage.
articles.description: A officer said the suspect shot himself while barricaded inside an apartment. He added that the man apparently had a dispute with the building’s homeowners association

articles.headline: ISRO successfully conducts ground static test of PSLV third stage
articles.title: ISRO successfully carries out ground static test of PSLV third stage
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation successfully executed a ground static test of the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle third stage at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota on November 12, 2026. The test followed anomalies in previous missions, prompting the space agency to strengthen nozzle configurations, improve design margins, and enhance quality checks and assembly procedures for the solid motor stage.
articles.description: The configuration of the third stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far

articles.headline: Comptroller and Auditor General to table integrated audit reports in December
articles.title: CAG to table first integrated audit reports in December, covering MSMEs and logistics
articles.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India adopted an integrated auditing approach to assess interconnected sectors collectively rather than individually. According to Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General K.S. Subramanian, the inaugural reports will be presented in December and will focus specifically on ease of doing business for micro, small, and medium enterprises alongside logistics across departments.
articles.description: The first of these reports would focus on ease of doing business and logistics.

articles.headline: Earthshot Prize CEO Jason Knauf praises India's renewable energy transformation
articles.title: India undergoing massive transformation in renewable energy: Earthshot Prize CEO
articles.summary: Jason Knauf, CEO of the Earthshot Prize, stated that India is undergoing a massive transformation in renewable energy during an interview on November 12, 2026. He spoke ahead of the five-day Earthshot Prize summit in Mumbai and Jaipur running from November 13 to 17, 2026, noting that the event founded by Prince William is being held in India for the first time to celebrate local climate innovations.
articles.description: “There is a race on right now. The first country that can have access to cheap, clean and abundant energy, is going to have a huge economic advantage. And India knows that,” says Jason Knauf

articles.headline: Comptroller and Auditor General begins comprehensive audit of power distribution companies
articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India has launched a comprehensive audit of 39 power distribution companies to assess financial and operational performance from fiscal years 2021 to 2026. The review includes direct engagement with 10,000 consumers to evaluate service quality. Findings will be reported to state legislatures to guide future national power policy interventions.
articles.description: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.

articles.headline: Hyderabad police launch artificial intelligence platform to map criminal networks
articles.title: Hyderabad Police launch AI platform to map accused persons and criminal networks
articles.summary: Hyderabad City Police introduced an in-house artificial intelligence system called Dooradrishti to consolidate records and analyze criminal networks. Commissioner V.C. Sajjanar unveiled the intelligence platform at the Integrated Command and Control Centre on November 12, 2026. The technology aims to reduce manual data collection time, accelerate investigations, and support intelligence-led preventive policing across the city.

articles.headline: AI chatbots recommend fake retail websites in study by Podqi
articles.title: AI chatbots are recommending fake retail websites, study finds
articles.summary: A study by intellectual property protection firm Podqi found that artificial intelligence chatbots displayed risky URLs in up to fifteen percent of shopping conversations. Testing Gemini, Perplexity, and ChatGPT with queries about one hundred fifty-one brands, researchers discovered Perplexity performed worst while Google Gemini showed risky sites least often. Representatives for the tech companies emphasized ongoing efforts to improve model accuracy and user safety.
articles.description: Shoppers using AI chatbots to research products or find places to buy items could be directed to imposters and other risky websites, a new study found. The study conducted by IP protection firm Podqi and shared exclusively with The Verge prompted ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity with a handful of shopping-related questions involving a selection of […]

articles.headline: US charges three men for allegedly plotting attack on UK base
articles.title: US charges three men for allegedly plotting attack on UK base
articles.description: The US has charged three men over alleged involvement in a plot to attack a Royal Air Force Base in Fairford, UK.

articles.headline: French authorities deny entry to prominent Israeli settler Yossi Dagan
articles.title: Prominent Israeli settler denied entry into France
articles.summary: French authorities denied entry to Yossi Dagan, head of an organization representing illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, at a Paris airport. Israel denounced the administrative ban as completely unacceptable and based on political grounds. The French ministry stated the measure stemmed from Dagan's active role in implementing settlement policy, which contradicts international law and undermines the two-state solution.
articles.description: Israel criticises Yossi Dagan's entry ban, labelling it 'unacceptable' amid tensions over illegal settlement policies.

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 11,000 cases
articles.title: Ebola cases in DR Congo pass 11,000, with 5,387 deaths
articles.summary: Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 11,042 alongside 5,387 deaths, according to government data released on Tuesday. Health authorities are struggling to contain the rare Bundibugyo strain across eight provinces amid delayed detection, conflict, and strained health services. This marks the second-largest outbreak on record, with containment further hindered by the current lack of specific vaccines or treatments.
articles.description: Authorities struggling to contain DRC's largest Ebola outbreak due to delayed detection and conflict.

articles.headline: Life insurers report 26 percent increase in new business premiums for October
articles.title: Life insurers’ new business premium rose 26% to ₹42,914 cr. in October
articles.summary: Life insurers recorded a 26 percent year-on-year rise in new business premiums to 42,914 crore rupees in October, according to the Life Insurance Council. State-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India saw a 31 percent increase, while private firms grew by 19 percent. Despite higher premiums, the total number of policies issued during the month declined.
articles.description: The policies/schemes issued by the life insurers in October was lower at 18,82,243 (19,53,996).

articles.headline: Russia intercepts 146 drones in Leningrad region during ongoing escalation
articles.title: Russia, Ukraine exchange strikes as Baltic nations issue drone alerts
articles.summary: Russian authorities reported shooting down 146 drones over the Leningrad region on Tuesday and Wednesday, causing a fire in Ust-Luga and following a refinery strike in Kirishi. Governor Aleksandr Drozdenko stated counter-action is ongoing. The escalation coincides with United States-mediated peace talks in Abu Dhabi and heightened security warnings across Latvia and Lithuania regarding unidentified drones entering Baltic airspace.
articles.description: Attacks also reported in Russia's northwest as US-mediated talks continue in Abu Dhabi.

articles.headline: Traffic accident in Fujairah leaves 14 dead and 30 injured
articles.title: UAE says 14 killed, 30 injured in Fujairah traffic accident
articles.summary: A major collision involving 18 vehicles and five trucks occurred at the entrance to Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, late Thursday. According to the Interior Ministry, a truck driver lost control, triggering a pile-up and fire. The 14 fatalities include Emirati nationals and foreigners, while 15 injured individuals remain hospitalized following the multi-vehicle crash incident.
articles.description: Officials say a driver lost control of his truck, causing a collision and fire involving 23 vehicles.

articles.headline: Bangladesh seeks extradition of ousted leader Sheikh Hasina from India
articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return to Bangladesh: the hurdles, the risks and the politics | Explained
articles.summary: Acting Foreign Minister Humayun Kabir announced that Bangladesh is seeking the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina through an acceptable prisoner transfer process after she applied for a new passport and national identity card in Dhaka on November 9, 2026. Hasina has been living in India since August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising, and faces a death sentence by the International Crimes Tribunal for a deadly police crackdown.
articles.description: Sheikh Hasina faces a dilemma. She wants to return as a political leader and reclaim her party, the Awami League. But she stands accused of ordering the police crackdown of July-August 2024, and the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) in Dhaka has sentenced her to death for it

articles.headline: BDS claims win as energy giants quit Israeli gas project off Gaza
articles.title: BDS claims win as energy giants quit Israeli gas project off Gaza
articles.description: The Boycott, Divest and Sanctions movement is claiming victory after a company left an Israeli-led gas project off Gaza.

articles.headline: Section 219: the future of US-Israeli defence partnership
articles.title: Section 219: the future of US-Israeli defence partnership
articles.description: US President Donald Trump has announced plans to end the billions of dollars in annual US military aid to Israel.

articles.headline: Oil India reports net profit doubling alongside interim dividend announcement
articles.title: Oil India net profit more the doubles on better realisations, higher output
articles.summary: State-owned Oil India Limited announced that its standalone net profit for the September quarter surpassed two thousand crore rupees, driven by increased crude oil production and better price realisations. The firm declared an interim dividend of seven rupees per equity share as operational revenue rose significantly alongside improved refinery margins from its subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery Limited.
articles.description: Oil India declared an interim dividend of ₹7 per equity share.

articles.headline: Four people shot in Washington DC
articles.title: Four people shot in Washington DC
articles.description: A major police operation is underway in Washington DC where four people have reportedly been shot

articles.headline: Centre receives twenty-two bids for advanced chemistry cell battery manufacturing
articles.title: Centre receives 22 bids for 10 GWh giga-scale ACC battery manufacturing capacity
articles.summary: The Ministry of Heavy Industries received twenty-two proposals for ten gigawatt-hours of grid-scale battery manufacturing capacity under a production-linked incentive scheme. Major corporations including Reliance Industries and Vikram Solar submitted bids to build domestic Advanced Chemistry Cell production, supporting national self-reliance goals and reducing import dependence for energy storage components.
articles.description: It forms part of the government’s broader target of establishing 50 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage.

articles.headline: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick
articles.title: Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick
articles.description: Michael Carrick has become the third recent Manchester United manager to be sacked midway through the season.

articles.headline: Iran opens training camp for women in readiness for war
articles.title: Iran opens training camp for women in readiness for war
articles.description: Iran has opened its first all-women military training camp amid fears of renewed US attacks.

articles.headline: World leaders gather for climate summit in Turkiye
articles.title: World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing
articles.summary: Dozens of heads of state and government officials are scheduled to speak during the high-level segment of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkiye. While leaders including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva are attending, several prominent G7 figures are noticeably absent from the annual United Nations summit.
articles.description: COP31 host Turkiye is championing a voluntary initiative to accelerate the electrification of transport, buildings and industry, with a target of raising electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35% by 2035

articles.headline: UK court convicts two Iranian men for spying on journalists
articles.title: UK court finds two Iranian men guilty of spying for Iran
articles.summary: Mostafa Sepahvand and Farhad Javadi Manesh were found guilty at Woolwich Crown Court of spying for Iran. The pair conducted surveillance on journalists and a lawyer in the United Kingdom. Prosecutors stated the men were promised rewards for intelligence gathering. The defendants are scheduled for sentencing at the Old Bailey on December 17 for their actions.
articles.description: The pair were promised rewards to send intelligence back to Iran, while one was prepared to commit a 'violent attack'.

articles.headline: Spanish parliament approves housing reforms following nationwide strike
articles.title: Spain approves housing reforms after nationwide strike over costs
articles.summary: Spain’s parliament ratified new decrees to limit evictions and curb real estate speculation after a nationwide general strike. The measures protect vulnerable tenants from eviction if no alternative housing is provided. However, the opposition Popular Party has vowed to repeal the laws if they win the upcoming snap election scheduled for later in November.
articles.description: Spanish parliament passes new laws limiting evictions but their duration depends on the upcoming snap election outcome.

articles.headline: Right-wing populism faces potential global shift as political dynamics evolve
articles.title: Is right-wing populism set to retreat?
articles.summary: Right-wing populism surged following the 2008 financial crisis by targeting ruling elites, capitalism, and immigrants while strengthening executive authority in democracies. Donald Trump amplified this movement globally by supporting leaders in Brazil, El Salvador, and Hungary. Observers note that political equations worldwide could change if the former United States president experiences a political weakening.
articles.description: Does the Republicans’ historic defeat in the midterm elections in the United States signal a waning of right-wing populism? Does the right’s emphasis on immigration and foreigners as political issues have an impact on voters? How will the anger of young protesters in India, France and other countries find political expression?

articles.headline: El Salvador fires missiles on Haitian gang hideout
articles.title: El Salvador fires missiles on Haitian gang hideout
articles.description: El Salvador’s military fired rockets at a compound allegedly belonging to the leader of Haiti’s 400 Mawozo gang.

articles.headline: House panel report details federal failures in Jeffrey Epstein sex crimes case
articles.title: GOP-led House report slams systemic failures in handling of Epstein case
articles.summary: The United States House of Representatives Committee on Oversight and Government Reform released a 137-page report on Tuesday condemning federal negligence in handling Jeffrey Epstein's case. Republican lawmakers criticized a 2007 non-prosecution agreement and jail monitoring lapses preceding his 2019 death. The committee urged the Department of Justice to re-interview witnesses, investigate associates, and ensure survivor record access.
articles.description: Decades of preferential treatment shielded Epstein and his associates, GOP-led report finds.

articles.headline: Indian scientists identify new deep-sea shark species in Indian Ocean
articles.title: New shark species identified in Indian Ocean after decades of misclassification
articles.summary: Researchers in India identified a distinct deep-sea shark species named Echinorhinus roinee, or the Indian Bramble Shark, previously misclassified as its Atlantic counterpart for decades. Scientists from the Zoological Survey of India and the Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute confirmed the discovery through physical measurements and DNA tests on specimens collected at Sakthikulangara Fishing Harbour in Kerala.
articles.description: The researchers identified the species Indian Bramble Shark, named Echinorhinus roinee

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy expresses satisfaction with US diplomatic messages on ending war
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy says he is pleased with messages from U.S. envoys on diplomatic efforts to end war
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated on November 10, 2026, that he was very pleased with messages from United States presidential envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff regarding the ongoing conflict with Russia. Speaking in Denmark after discussions wrapped up in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Zelenskyy emphasized the critical sequence of achieving a ceasefire before establishing European security guarantees.
articles.description: “I see changes. I am very happy about what I hear,” Mr. Zelenskyy said when asked about the recent messages by U.S. presidential ‌envoys ⁠Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff

articles.headline: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocates to military base following Iranian threats
articles.title: U.S. Treasury chief Bessent moved to military base after Iranian threats, reports say
articles.summary: United States Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently moved out of his home and onto a military base due to advanced Iranian threats against his life, according to a report published on November 10, 2026, by the New York Times. The security measure occurred amid heightened tensions and an ongoing economic pressure campaign against Tehran during the U.S.-Israeli war.
articles.description: Iran has previously denied plotting to attack ‌officials and people on U.S. soil

articles.headline: Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader following midterm election losses
articles.title: Trump ally Jim Jordan elected U.S. House Republican leader after midterm election rout
articles.summary: On November 10, 2026, U.S. Representative Jim Jordan of Ohio was elected leader of House Republicans, defeating Steve Scalise by 106 votes to 73. Mr. Jordan will replace outgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson as the leader of the party's opposition following significant defeats in the midterm elections that cost Republicans control of Congress.
articles.description: The Ohio Congressman will replace House Speaker Mike Johnson, who announced he was stepping down from leadership after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress

articles.headline: Delhi voter deletion applications concentrate on three Muslim neighborhoods
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Why BJP BLAs’ voter deletion applications in Mustafabad focused on three neighbourhoods
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party-appointed booth level agents filed 796 voter deletion applications in Delhi's Mustafabad that were concentrated across 25 polling booths in Nehru Vihar, Dayalpur, and Chandu Nagar. According to an analysis of records and local interviews by The Hindu published on November 10, 2026, all targeted electors were Muslim and selected from areas with sizeable populations and few initial draft roll deletions.
articles.description: 796 Form 7 applications against Muslims, filed by 20 BJP BLAs, concentrated on the rolls of 25 polling booths in Mustafabad. However, BJP claims it has not directed the filing of these applications

articles.headline: Police report at least five people shot in central Washington
articles.title: At least five people shot, one killed, in central Washington, DC
articles.summary: Law enforcement officials confirmed that at least five individuals sustained gunshot wounds near Logan Circle in Washington, District of Columbia, prompting area schools to enter lockdown and a shelter-in-place order. Local and federal agencies responded to the incident occurring approximately one mile from the White House, while the administration of United States President Donald Trump continued its focus on urban crime.
articles.description: Authorities say the suspected shooter has been apprehended, after he shot himself.

articles.headline: Scott Colom becomes Mississippi's first Black US senator in over 150 years
articles.title: Before Scott Colom, these two men were the last black US senators from Mississippi
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom won a close election in Mississippi, becoming the state's first Black US senator since 1875 and only the third in its history. He follows Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce, who served during the Reconstruction era before Jim Crow laws were enacted. Colom secured victory by mobilizing young voters and the state's Black population.
articles.description: The Democratic candidate won in a southern state that had not seated a black senator since 1874.

articles.headline: Colombian air strike kills eight people including senior gang leader
articles.title: Eight killed in Colombian air strike targeting Gulf Clan gang
articles.summary: Colombian armed forces conducted a bombing in the north-western province of Antioquia that resulted in eight deaths, according to President Abelardo de la Espriella. The operation targeted the Gulf Clan and successfully eliminated Haminton Mosquera, who was accused of orchestrating attacks on law enforcement. The president vowed to continue military operations to reclaim territory from criminal groups involved in cocaine trafficking and extortion.
articles.description: A suspected gang leader considered a "priority target" was among those killed, the Colombian president says.

articles.headline: US charges three men over alleged terrorist plot targeting UK air base
articles.title: US charges 3 men over alleged Iranian-backed plot at UK Fairford air base
articles.summary: United States prosecutors have charged three men with terrorism-related offenses for allegedly planning attacks across the US and Europe, including a plot targeting the United Kingdom air base RAF Fairford. According to the Department of Justice, the suspects acted in support of Iran and Iraq groups. The UK incident led the US military to withdraw aircraft from British bases.
articles.description: The men, including one who is already in jail, face charges over alleged plot at UK air base used in US war on Iran.

articles.headline: Republicans block Hegseth impeachment motion
articles.title: Republicans block Hegseth impeachment motion
articles.description: Republicans have blocked a motion to impeach US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth over the war on Iran.

articles.headline: House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over handling of Epstein records
articles.title: U.S. House Oversight Committee criticises Trump administration over release of Epstein records
articles.summary: On November 10, 2026, the Republican-led House Oversight Committee released a report criticising the Trump administration for failing to properly manage the public release of millions of pages of records relating to Jeffrey Epstein. According to the committee, missed deadlines, inadequate redactions that exposed survivors' sensitive information, and concealed names of alleged co-conspirators marred the disclosure process mandated by the Epstein Files Transparency Act.
articles.description: The 137-page report, released by the GOP-controlled committee, comes nearly a year after Congress passed and President Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act

articles.headline: House Republicans derail impeachment resolution targeting Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title: U.S. Republicans derail bid to impeach Hegseth
articles.summary: Republicans in the United States House of Representatives blocked an impeachment resolution targeting Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on November 10, 2026. The 211 to 204 vote sent the measure to the Judiciary Committee, averting a formal floor vote. Representative Thomas Massie introduced the articles over unauthorised military actions, while Pentagon officials and President Donald Trump strongly dismissed the allegations.
articles.description: The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee; this halts the immediate impeachment drive but does not prevent Democrats from reviving the effort after taking control of Congress in January

articles.headline: Italian schools receive mass bomb threats for second consecutive day
articles.title: More than 1,800 Italian schools targeted by new hoax bomb alerts
articles.summary: More than 1,800 schools across Italy received email bomb threats on Thursday, following 6,300 similar alerts the previous day. Authorities confirmed the messages were hoaxes, noting they were signed by a purported leader of the Vilayat of Misoginistan. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has called for coordination to address rising concerns regarding hybrid warfare and cyberthreats.
articles.description: The latest warnings come amid rising concerns ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠in Europe about hybrid warfare threats.

articles.headline: Building collapse in Brooklyn construction site leaves two people dead
articles.title: New York building collapse: At least 8 people dead as rescuers dig through rubble
articles.summary: A three-story building in the Flatbush section of Brooklyn collapsed into an adjacent construction pit on Wednesday, resulting in at least two fatalities and multiple injuries. Emergency responders utilized power saws, drones, and rescue dogs to search through the rubble for trapped survivors. Mayor Zohran Mamdani issued a statement asking the community to support affected neighbors during ongoing rescue operations.
articles.description: The collapse cause was under investigation, but NYC buildings commissioner Ahmed Tigani said workers were excavating an empty lot next door for a new building when it fell

articles.headline: Displaced Tigray families face renewed uncertainty as fighting escalates in Ethiopia
articles.title: Tigray displaced families fear renewed war as hopes of returning home fade
articles.summary: Families displaced from Western Tigray and currently sheltering in Abi Adi continue to struggle with shortages of food, clean water, and medicine. Four years after the signing of the Pretoria agreement, renewed fighting that began in September 2026 has deepened uncertainty for displaced residents, while thousands of former fighters undergo rehabilitation training in Mekelle.
articles.description: Displaced families face renewed uncertainty as fighting returns to Tigray.

articles.headline: Senate Republicans reelect John Thune as leader despite midterm election defeats
articles.title: U.S. Senate Republicans vote to keep John Thune as leader after steep midterm election losses
articles.summary: On November 11, 2026, United States Senate Republicans reelected South Dakota Senator John Thune as their leader following steep midterm election losses that cost the party its majority. Despite internal frustrations and a 31-15 vote over a delay attempt, no alternative candidates emerged to challenge Mr. Thune for the position during the closed-door meetings.
articles.description: South Dakota Sen. John Thune has spent much of the last two years navigating President Trump, who has often been at odds with the Senate

articles.headline: FIFA confirms Under-17 World Cup will proceed in Qatar
articles.title: FIFA Under-17 World Cup to kick off in Qatar despite US withdrawal
articles.summary: FIFA announced the Under-17 World Cup will begin in Qatar on November 19 as scheduled, despite the United States Soccer Federation withdrawing its team. The US cited safety concerns linked to a Level 3 travel advisory regarding regional conflict. FIFA stated its security assessments remain unchanged and that it is prepared for the 48-team tournament.
articles.description: FIFA says its 'security assessments' for the 48-team tournament remain unchanged after US Soccer pulled out.

articles.headline: Canada bars Russian athletes from entering for World Junior Championship
articles.title: Canada won’t let Russian players enter for ice hockey junior championship
articles.summary: Canada will prevent Russian and Belarusian athletes and officials from entering the country for the upcoming World Junior Championship in Alberta. Secretary of State for Sport Adam van Koeverden stated the government opposes their participation due to the ongoing war in Ukraine. The tournament is scheduled to take place from December 26 to January 5.
articles.description: Russian, Belarusian athletes and officials will be prevented from entering Canada regardless of their visa status.

articles.headline: Greta Thunberg: The planet is being killed
articles.title: Greta Thunberg: The planet is being killed
articles.description: Climate activist Greta Thunberg delivers a stark warning at COP31.

articles.headline: Spain holds state funeral for 69 victims of deadly train crash
articles.title: Spain holds state funeral for 69 victims of deadly train crash
articles.description: Spain’s King and Queen have joined families of the 69 victims from a deadly train collision at a state funeral.

articles.headline: Documentary examines influence of Christian Zionism on United States policy
articles.title: ‘Greater Israel’: Christian Zionism’s role in US policy
articles.summary: A new Al Jazeera documentary explores how Christian Zionism has evolved from a theological belief into a significant political force in the United States. The film details how evangelical support and lobbying efforts influence US foreign policy regarding Israel. It highlights the role of organizations like Christians United for Israel in shaping modern political discourse.
articles.description: Israel, the US, Christian Zionism and the search for Armageddon.

articles.headline: US judge allows Donald Trump defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
articles.title: U.S. judge says Trump’s $10 billion BBC defamation case can proceed
articles.summary: A United States federal judge in Florida ruled on November 10, 2026, that President Donald Trump can proceed with a ten billion dollar defamation lawsuit against the BBC regarding a deceptively edited speech clip. Judge Jeffrey Kuntz dismissed an unfair trade practices claim while finding the defamation allegations plausible. The BBC previously admitted the edits were misleading and apologised.
articles.description: U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz in Florida declined to throw out Mr. Trump’s defamation ​claim against the BBC, ‌saying Mr. Trump had plausibly alleged that the broadcaster damaged his reputation and knew or should have known the clip was misleading

articles.headline: Ladakh Police remove activist Sonam Wangchuk from protest site in Leh
articles.title: Ladakh elections row: Sonam Wangchuk removed from protest site, escorted to residence by Police
articles.summary: Ladakh Police removed climate activist Sonam Wangchuk from a protest site in Leh and escorted him home on November 11, 2026. Authorities advised him to stay indoors under prohibitory orders issued by the Chief Electoral Officer and District Magistrate. The action followed protests by Wangchuk and regional bodies opposing hill council elections scheduled for December 4 due to severe winter conditions and seasonal migration.
articles.description: Mr. Wangchuk is protesting the holding of hill council elections on December 4, citing harsh winter conditions and large-scale seasonal migration

articles.headline: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng blocked from entering India for Bharat Summit
articles.title: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng says she has been stopped from coming to Hyderabad for Bharat Summit
articles.summary: Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng stated that orders from India's Ministry of Home Affairs cancelled her valid visa, preventing her from attending the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen, was invited as a speaker on press freedom. She linked the entry denial to a question she previously asked Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Norway.
articles.description: Ms. Lyng says she has been denied entry into India despite having a visa

articles.headline: Pakistan releases two sisters of former Prime Minister Imran Khan
articles.title: Pakistan releases two sisters of ex-PM Imran Khan from jail
articles.summary: Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi Khan were released from Kot Lakhpat prison in Lahore on Thursday after 53 days of detention. Their brother, former Prime Minister Imran Khan, remains incarcerated since August 2023. The government previously detained the sisters citing potential threats to law and order ahead of a planned political protest by the PTI party.
articles.description: Uzma and Noreen released from a Lahore jail but Aleema Khan still detained nearly two months after their arrest.

articles.headline: Venezuela asserts sovereign right to expand oil production at COP31
articles.title: Venezuela tells COP31 it has sovereign right to pump more oil
articles.summary: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the COP31 climate summit on November 12, 2026, that Venezuela maintains the right to develop its oil industry. While acknowledging climate change, she argued that economic growth and environmental protection can coexist. The stance aligns with United States efforts to boost Venezuelan oil output to enhance Western Hemisphere energy security.
articles.description: Venezuela’s Acting President ​Delcy Rodriguez’s comments at the UN ‌talks on Turkiye’s Mediterranean coast jar with efforts by other conference leaders to convince global governments to accelerate a ‌shift from carbon-emitting fossil fuels

articles.headline: Scott Colom becomes Mississippi's first Black senator in 150 years
articles.title: Who is Scott Colom, Mississippi’s first Black senator in 150 years?
articles.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith to become the first Black senator from Mississippi since 1874. The narrow victory, confirmed on Wednesday, marks the first Democratic Senate win in the state in 43 years. Colom, a former prosecutor, campaigned on affordability and wage growth, securing a seat that shifts the Senate balance to 55-44.
articles.description: Mississippi is home to a large Black American population but no Black person has held a Senate seat since the 1800s.

articles.headline: Alice Huang visited Taiwan eight times during 2024 and 2025
articles.title: Alice Huang, accused of spying on Nvidia chief, entered Taiwan eight times in 2024-25: Official
articles.summary: Alice Huang, an executive accused of spying for Beijing while linked to Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, entered Taiwan eight times between 2024 and 2025 using a Hong Kong passport, according to Mainland Affairs Council Minister Chiu Chui-cheng on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Taiwanese officials stated she entered under standard business visitor status and security agencies are currently investigating the matter.
articles.description: Taiwan, a dominant player in the global semiconductor industry, sits at the centre of strategic competition between the United States and China, which claims the self-ruled island as part of its territory

articles.headline: Megaspeed pledges cooperation with US probe into Nvidia CEO scandal
articles.title: Megaspeed to cooperate with U.S. probe into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang scandal
articles.summary: Singapore-headquartered technology firm Megaspeed announced on November 12, 2026, that it will fully cooperate with United States investigations regarding national security risks. The statement followed Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang admitting to a past relationship with a former executive of the company, as Nvidia board members reportedly met to discuss the unfolding situation.
articles.description: Megaspeed, in a statement on November 12, said that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously

articles.headline: US Justice Department charges three Iranian operatives over British airbase plot
articles.title: U.S. charges three ‘Iranian operatives’ over U.K. airbase plot
articles.summary: The United States Justice Department announced an eight-count indictment on November 10, 2026, against three men identified as Iranian operatives for allegedly planning a terrorist plot at Britain Royal Air Force Fairford airbase in September. Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri, and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani faced charges involving material support for terrorism, conspiracy, and attempted destruction of property.
articles.description: Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, Mohsen Mohajeri and Mohammad Ali al-Hassani allegedly helped plan and direct the September incident at Britain’s RAF Fairford airbase

articles.headline: Scientists discover five new miniature frog species in eastern Himalayas
articles.title: Five new miniature frog species found in eastern Himalayas
articles.summary: Researchers from the University of Delhi and Harvard University have identified five new species of tiny horned frogs in India's eastern Himalayas. Published in the Royal Society Open Science journal on November 11, the study reveals the region as a significant biodiversity hotspot. One discovery, the snail-eating horned frog, is the first known species to consume snails.
articles.description: Scientists say the frogs evolved as the Himalayas rose and the Asian monsoon took shape.

articles.headline: Farooq Abdullah urges India-Pakistan dialogue to resolve disputes
articles.title: Will be too late by the time guns fall silent: Farooq Abdullah pushes for India-Pakistan dialogue
articles.summary: National Conference President Farooq Abdullah asserted on November 12, 2026, that military confrontation cannot resolve political disputes between India and Pakistan. Speaking in Jammu and Kashmir, the former chief minister called for immediate engagement without waiting for hostilities to cease, while emphasizing that the region remains an integral part of India despite persistent security threats.
articles.description: The former Chief Minister also asserted that Kashmir is, was and will remain an integral part of India

articles.headline: Nvidia hires law firm to investigate CEO affair with alleged spy
articles.title: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
articles.summary: Nvidia has appointed New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to examine a romantic relationship between Chief Executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singaporean executive at customer firm Megaspeed whom the US government alleges is a Chinese spy. The independent probe runs alongside an FBI investigation as the company faces scrutiny and falling stock market values.
articles.description: The appointment was made after it emerged Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

articles.headline: Woman loses arm after being pushed from Naigaon railway station platform
articles.title: Woman loses arm after being pushed off platform at Naigaon railway station; suspect arrested
articles.summary: A 20-year-old woman lost her left arm on November 4, 2026, after being pushed into the gap between two train coaches at Naigaon railway station. According to police statements, the victim confronted a 53-year-old man named Jitendra Hirmukhe for molestation before being shoved. Authorities examined closed-circuit television footage and arrested the suspect on November 9 under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
articles.description: The police arrested the accused after examining CCTV footage on November 9, and booked him under Sections 117 (2), 74, and 352 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.headline: Authorities demolish alleged illegal mosque in Sambhal district
articles.title: Demolition of 'illegal' mosque in U.P.’s Sambhal village under way amid heavy police deployment
articles.summary: Officials began demolishing an alleged illegal mosque in Qutubpur Satta village within the Asmoli area of Sambhal district on November 12, 2026. Circle Officer Aman Singh stated that a joint team inspected the public land site before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate ordered the action. Heavy police deployment, drone monitoring, and security forces were implemented to maintain peace.
